html:
SMTO-ART-0027 — SMTO couldn't find that saved result in the chosen conversation

GUID: 687b423f-d67a-417f-ba79-ef3d52e4c8ca
Slug: artifact-reference-scope-invalid
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • The saved result you tried to use either belongs to a different conversation than the one named, or it has since been deleted. SMTO couldn't use it, so nothing was attached.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the message box, type @artifact: and choose the result from the list that appears. That list only shows saved results SMTO can still find, with the right conversation already filled in.
  2. If you used Add context › Link existing context, check that the Source conversation, Artifact run and reference were all copied from the same conversation. SMTO only links a result when its Run belongs to the conversation you named.
  3. If the original conversation or Task was deleted, its saved results are gone. Ask SMTO to produce that result again in this conversation instead. Results from deleted conversations can't be shared, and SMTO won't quietly swap in a similar result from elsewhere.

What success looks like

  • The result shows as attached to your message, and the message sends without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the conversation you were linking from, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't attach a look-alike result from another conversation unless it's the one you really want.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Resource linking or result lookup failed because the source Run is not part of the named source conversation, or no non-deleted result exists for that run and reference.

What this means

  • Resource linking cannot establish the source run's conversation membership, or receipt lookup finds no artifact under the selected run/reference. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Resource linking cannot establish the source run's conversation membership, or receipt lookup finds no artifact under the selected run/reference.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact source conversation/run membership and retained identity before linking.

How to fix it

  • POST /api/agent/context/link requires source_run_id to be one of conversation_runs(source_conversation_id), and RunStore.get(run_id, reference, retained=True) / MemoryRunStore.get_in must resolve the artifact or an explicit artifact link whose runs still exist and are not tombstoned. Re-select the reference through the @artifact: picker or correct the conversation/run/reference triple; never substitute another run's artifact.
  • Select a retained artifact from the owning scope, or explicitly link it through the supported context flow when permitted.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported authorized link or current retained reference resolves the intended artifact.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
